historical_growth.growth_rate_source: year-1 base-case judgment from FY2026 guidance and the Q4-2026 exit rate (not equity CAGR, see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (38.3%) exceeds revenue 3-yr CAGR (26.9%) by more than 30% relative. Book equity growth is almost entirely additional paid-in capital from stock compensation (APIC +805 in 9M-2026 against net income of 215), not retained earnings, so it is not a usable growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue: FY2020 603.5, FY2022 1,675.1, FY2025 3,427.2. EPS CAGRs are undefined: GAAP EPS was negative in FY2020 and FY2022. Owner-FCF series (company FCF less total SBC less interest income): FY2023 597.5 - 495.9 - 103.5 = -1.9; FY2024 775.1 - 583.5 - 155.3 = +36.3; FY2025 914.7 - 774.1 - 194.4 = -53.8; TTM Sep-2026 +20.5. The series crosses zero so no CAGR is meaningful, and that is the finding: reported FCF compounded at ~24% a year FY2023-FY2025 while owner FCF stayed at roughly nil, because SBC (21-23% of revenue) and interest income grew as fast as the cash flow.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 grows 22% off the 4,520 guided FY2026 base: the Q4-2026 guide already implies ~25% year on year with the largest customer (widely reported as OpenAI) at its contractual minimum, net revenue retention holds near 120% on cross-sell (61% of customers on 4+ products, 41% on 6+), but new-logo adds have slowed to a few hundred a quarter and the AI-native cohort stops being a tailwind. Growth then fades about two points a year to 6% in FY2036, for ~15.6bn of revenue against a Gartner observability market of ~39bn in 2029. The pre-SBC EBITDA margin rises from ~24% to 32% as the business matures, a little above the Q3-2026 peak quarter, and SBC falls from ~20% of revenue to 12%, roughly 0.8pp a year, faster than the house default because hiring slows with growth but still well above large mature software peers. The owner-FCF margin ends near 13%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The largest-customer step-down proves a one-off rather than a template: other AI-native customers keep expanding, LLM Observability, Bits AI SRE and the security and product-analytics modules give the cross-sell engine a second leg, and enterprise consolidation onto one platform keeps retention above 120%. Revenue grows 28% in FY2027 and is still at 8% in FY2036 (~22bn). Usage-based operating leverage shows through, with pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaching 37% and SBC falling to 10% of revenue as the share price does more of the retention work. This needs both the AI workload tailwind and sustained margin discipline, which is why it is weighted below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: The largest customer is the template: AI labs and the biggest cloud-native customers bring observability in-house or onto open-source and hyperscaler-native tooling, usage optimisation spreads across the 91% of ARR held by 100k+ customers, and growth falls to 16% in FY2027 and mid-single digits by the end of the horizon (~10bn revenue). Third-party cloud hosting costs keep compressing gross margin (79% vs 80% a year earlier), so pre-SBC EBITDA margin only reaches 28%, while a lower share price forces SBC to stay at 14-15% of revenue to retain engineers. Terminal growth 2.5% and a 15x cap reflect a slower, more commoditised business.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Datadog is a high-quality, net-cash platform business whose reported free cash flow (~1.1bn trailing) is almost exactly equal to its stock compensation plus the interest on its cash. On the house basis, with SBC expensed and the share count held flat, trailing owner FCF is roughly nil, and value comes from the margin and SBC-intensity paths over the next decade plus 4.2bn of net cash. The street basis, which treats SBC as non-cash, is reported alongside; the gap between the two is the measure of how much of the market price rests on that accounting choice.
key_risks_to_valuation: SBC intensity is the single most sensitive driver: each point of terminal SBC % of revenue moves value materially, and the base case assumes it falls from ~20% to 12% without a management commitment to that path
Largest-customer and AI-native cohort concentration: Q4-2026 guidance assumes the top customer at its contractual minimum; further optimisation by other large usage-based customers is the bear axis
Terminal margin: base 32% pre-SBC EBITDA margin is above anything yet reported for a full year (FY2025 22%, Q3-2026 27.6%)
Gross-margin pressure from third-party cloud hosting costs growing faster than revenue
2029 convertible notes are treated as 1,000 of debt; above ~217.60 a share they convert into ~4.6m shares, partly offset by capped calls (relevant only on the street basis and in upside outcomes)
Acquisition spend (cash and stock) is outside the modelled flows

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular-session close); 52-week range 98.01-300.68
data_sources.financials: DDOG_Metrics.csv and DDOG.duckdb (XBRL); FY2025 10-K (DDOG_Annual_FY2025.txt: free cash flow reconciliation lines 2409-2412, SBC 2665/2687, cash taxes 2721); Q3-2026 10-Q (DDOG_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt: balance sheet 1294-1326, cash flow 1441-1483, EPS share table 2180-2199, SBC note 2121-2123, employer payroll taxes 2323-2335, FCF reconciliation 2573-2580)
data_sources.qualitative: DDOG_Analysis.json (2026-11-15), including Q3-2026 results and FY2026 / Q4-2026 guidance of 4 Nov 2026

inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30 Sep 2026 = FY2025 10-K total stock-based compensation 774.1 (statement of stockholders' equity, incl. 23.5 capitalised into internal-use software) less 9M-2025 560.6 plus 9M-2026 675.5 (Q3-2026 10-Q note, 'Total stock-based compensation expense'). Datadog does not net-share-settle (no equity-award withholding line in financing), so there is no award-tax add-on; employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions (63.5 in 9M-2026) are a cash operating cost already inside reported FCF and are kept inside the EBITDA margin definition used here.
inputs.share_count_basis: Period-end 30 Sep 2026: 337.21 Class A + 23.81 Class B = 361.02 basic, plus the Q3-2026 treasury-method dilution from the EPS note (options 1.39, ESPP 0.03, RSUs/PSUs 9.69, acquisition restricted stock 0.69) = 372.8. The 4.596 if-converted shares of the 2029 notes are EXCLUDED and the notes carried as 1,000 of debt at face instead (conversion price ~217.60 is above the market price; capped calls offset dilution above it up to the cap). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. US 10-year risk-free ~4.3% + 5.0% equity risk premium x beta ~1.15 = ~10% cost of equity; the company is net cash with a zero-coupon convertible, so WACC = cost of equity = 10%. Same rate in all three scenarios; risk is charged through the scenario weights, not through the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease expense sits inside operating costs and therefore inside the EBITDA margin. Operating lease liabilities (320.6) are NOT added to net debt. lease_cost_pct_path omitted (zero).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, via the Drivers route (dcf-methods routing row 1: operating SaaS company). First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF and no memory entry. FY0 = FY2026E at the midpoint of the 4 Nov 2026 guidance (revenue 4,515-4,525), because nine months of FY2026 are already in the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet; year 1 of the forecast is FY2027. last_fcf / reported_fcf / sbc / interest_income are TRAILING TWELVE MONTHS to 30 Sep 2026 (reported FCF, company definition = OCF less PP&E less capitalised software: 914.7 FY2025 - 623.7 9M-2025 + 818.4 9M-2026 = 1,109.4). Owner FCF = 1,109.4 - 889.0 SBC - 199.9 interest income = 20.5, i.e. essentially all of reported FCF is SBC plus interest on the cash pile. NOTE the Metrics.csv free_cash_flow column deducts PP&E only (FY2025 1,000.6) and overstates the company's own FCF (914.7) by the capitalised software spend. EBITDA margin definition used in the driver paths: GAAP operating income + D&A + expensed SBC, i.e. BEFORE SBC but AFTER employer payroll taxes on equity awards (~1.9% of revenue) -- about 0.3pp below the company's non-GAAP operating margin plus D&A. Actuals on that basis: FY2025 22.2%, 9M-2026 23.9%, Q3-2026 27.6%, FY2026E ~23.8% using the Q4 non-GAAP operating income guide of 280-290. Interest income is excluded from the forward flows by construction (the build starts from EBITDA) and the 5,233.6 of cash and marketable securities is added through net debt. Net cash = 881.2 cash + 4,352.4 marketable securities - 1,000.0 face of the 0% 2029 convertible notes. Non-repurchaser: no buyback cash in any period, the basic count has grown ~2.5-3% a year, so the flat share count is a modelling convention paid for by the SBC charge, not something the company funds. Acquisitions (115.6 cash plus 75.3 of restricted stock in 9M-2026) are not modelled. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

base.drivers_note: Capex includes capitalised software (FY2025 135.4 = 4.0% of revenue; 9M-2026 122.0 = 3.7%). D&A 1.75% of revenue in 9M-2026, rising as capitalised software amortises. Cash tax: 17.6 paid in FY2025 and 25.7 in 9M-2026 against a full valuation allowance of 543.1 on US deferred tax assets, so the rate ramps from ~10% to 22% as losses are absorbed rather than holding the shelter. Working capital: owner FCF less the component build implies roughly +5% of incremental revenue (deferred revenue inflow largely offset by receivables and capitalised commissions; usage billed monthly in arrears).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: usage-based revenue with a disclosed single-customer cut, and a growth mix that has leaned on a concentrated AI-native cohort, though there is no balance-sheet or solvency risk (4.2bn net cash). Base held at 50%: it follows guidance and the Q4 exit rate. Bull cut from 35% to 30%: it needs AI workloads to stay on the platform, cross-sell to stay strong, and margins to expand ten-plus points, three things that are not independent of the bear axis.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
